title: Practical Policies and Templates: Company-wide Operational Reference
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose: This page is a compact, operational reference that consolidates core company-wide policies and process templates used by people-ops, finance, engineering, and product teams. It is intended for implementers and approvers who need a single place to reference the required steps, ownership, thresholds, and example templates for: access and permissions, change management, data management, procurement and expenses, vendor management, travel policies, and basic process templates.

Scope: Applies to all Redwood Inference employees, contingent workers, and contractors unless an explicit exemption is granted by the policy owner listed below.

Owners and escalation

- Primary owner: People Operations (people-ops@redwood.com)
- Secondary owners: Finance & Legal for procurement/expenses, Security for access/data controls, Engineering for change management of production services
- Executive escalation: VP People / VP Finance as appropriate

How to use this page

1. Read the high-level policy section relevant to your task.
2. Use the included checklists and templates when submitting requests.
3. Route requests to the team-specific intake systems listed in Related Pages.

---

1) Access and Permissions (RBAC and onboarding offboarding)

Summary: Access is granted on a least-privilege basis and must be tied to a documented business justification. Role definitions are maintained in the central RBAC catalogue and reviewed quarterly. All interactive access is scoped by roles and temporary escalation is time-bound.

Key principles:
- Grant minimum privileges required and document justification in the ticket.
- Use group assignments for team-level permissions; avoid individual direct grants except for exec-level exceptions.
- All privileged access requests must include an owner and an expiration date.

Request process (quick steps):
1. Open an access request via the Access Management portal (link: /confluence/security-and-compliance/rbac-and-auth).
2. Select role or custom grant and paste business justification.
3. Manager approves within 48 hours; security reviews high-privilege grants within 72 hours.
4. Automation provisions access and triggers an audit log entry.

Approval matrix (examples):
- Standard dev tooling (GitHub, Slack): manager approval.
- Production infra (cloud console, staging clusters): manager + infra owner.
- Secrets/keys (KMS/HSM access): manager + security lead + quarterly review.

Temporary escalation template (example text for the request):
- Reason: Emergency hotfix for payment latency issue
- Scope: Grant "infra-ops:write" on production-cluster-alpha for 4 hours
- Owner: Jane Doe (SRE)
- Rollback: Revoke access at expiration; automatic revoke enforced by automation

Auditing and review
- Quarterly role review: team leads must confirm membership and justification.
- Annual privileged-access attestation: security sends attestations to employees with privileged roles.

---

2) Change Management (service and configuration changes)

Policy summary: All changes to production services, infra config, and provider integrations must follow the change management workflow. Low-risk changes follow a lightweight process; medium/high-risk changes require a scheduled maintenance window and a rollback plan.

Change categories:
- Low: Non-prod config, documentation changes, read-only dashboards
- Medium: Non-disruptive infra modifications, schema migrations with backward compatibility guarantees
- High: Any change that can impact availability, integrity, or data residency (e.g., production deploys without canary, DB migrations that rewrite historical data)

Change request template (required fields):
- Title
- Owner and approver (owner_team)
- Impact assessment (availability, latency, data integrity)
- Rollback plan and test criteria
- Scheduled window and blackout windows
- Post-deploy verification steps

Approval workflow (summary):
1. Submit CR in the Change Management system (internal ticketing).
2. Triage by change coordinator within 24 hours.
3. Low-risk: automated approval if owner signs off and no conflicts.
4. Medium/High-risk: schedule a review meeting with SRE, Security, Product owner.
5. Document deployment and verification; close the CR only after verification steps pass.

Canary and fallback policy:
- Canary releases are required for all model-serving rollouts exceeding 25% traffic or when model architecture changes.
- Fallback: auto-route to last-known-good model variant on errors >1% 5m error rate or latency >2x baseline for 5m.

---

3) Data Management (classification, retention, and handling)

Principles: Data must be classified, access-controlled, and handled according to sensitivity and jurisdictional requirements. The central data catalogue defines classification labels and retention periods.

Classification labels (short list):
- Public: safe to publish externally
- Internal: for employee use only
- Confidential: customer data, contracts, sensitive product telemetry
- Restricted: PII, PHI, or regulated data (requires encryption at rest + KMS/HSM keys)

Minimum handling rules:
- Confidential and Restricted data must not be stored in personal devices or public cloud buckets without encryption and approved controls.
- Logs containing sensitive tokens or PII must be redacted at ingestion or stored in a restricted index with 90-day retention by default.

Retention matrix (example):
| Data type | Classification | Default retention | Owner |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Application logs (error-level) | Internal | 90 days | Eng-SRE |
| Audit logs (access grants) | Restricted | 3 years | Security |
| Customer telemetry (anonymized) | Internal | 2 years | Product |
| Billing & invoices | Confidential | 7 years | Finance |

Data transfer and third-party processors:
- Any transfer of Restricted data to a third party requires a Data Processing Addendum (DPA) signed by Legal and a security assessment (high-level questionnaire + pentest history review).

---

4) Procurement and Expenses (vendor spend, credit cards, and employee reimbursements)

Principles: All spend is subject to approval thresholds and must follow the procurement lifecycle: request -> sourcing -> approvals -> PO/contract -> invoicing & payment. Cards and petty cash use follow the expense policy below.

Approval thresholds (examples):
- <= $1,000: manager approval; one-off purchase allowed via corporate card or expense request
- $1,001 - $25,000: manager + finance approval; must create PO
- > $25,000: manager + finance + legal; require vendor review and contract

Procurement checklist:
1. Validate budget line with your manager.
2. Check preferred vendor list.
3. Obtain at least 2 quotes for purchases > $10,000.
4. Submit PR and attach vendor alignment (security questionnaire if required).
5. Finance issues PO; procurement team completes vendor onboarding.

Expense submission template (required fields for reimbursements):
- Employee name
- Date of expense
- Category (travel/accommodation/meal/supplies)
- Amount (USD)
- Business justification
- Receipt attachment (required for all expenses)

Corporate card usage rules:
- No personal charges; any accidental personal charges must be reimbursed within 30 days and reported to Finance.

---

5) Vendor Management and Risk Assessments

Overview: Vendors are tiered by risk (low/medium/high). High-risk vendors (cloud infra, identity providers, payments) must complete an extended security assessment and maintain SOC2 or equivalent evidence.

Onboarding steps for new vendors (summary):
1. Business sponsor creates vendor intake ticket with use case and data types required.
2. Security runs a risk assessment (questionnaire + required evidence).
3. Legal reviews contract terms; Finance assigns a cost center.
4. Approval gates: high-risk requires Security + Legal + Finance sign-off.

Vendor review cadence:
- High-risk: quarterly check-ins and annual evidence update
- Medium-risk: bi-annual review
- Low-risk: annual automated healthcheck (APIs/uptime)

Termination checklist (for offboarding a vendor):
- Revoke credentials and API keys
- Ensure data return or deletion per contract
- Update asset inventory and notify stakeholders

---

6) Travel and Business Events

Policy summary: Travel is approved based on business need with pre-authorization required for trips over $500. Safety, cost-efficiency, and compliance with local regulations are required.

Booking guidance:
- Preferred travel vendors are listed in the procurement portal.
- Economy or standard class for domestic flights; business class considered for >8h flights with manager approval.
- Use corporate hotels where possible; per-night thresholds are published for major markets.

Pre-trip checklist:
1. Manager approves travel request in Travel system.
2. Employee books through approved vendor and attaches itinerary.
3. Submit travel advance if required >72 hours before departure.

Emergency and safety:
- Register trip with People Ops using the Trip Registration form.
- Emergency contact: people-ops@redwood.com. For high-risk geographies, additional approvals and security briefings are required.

---

7) Internal Templates (ready-to-use snippets)

Use the templates below as copy-paste content for ticketing systems and vendor intake forms. Always replace placeholders with real values.

A) Access Request template:
- Title: "Access: [System] - [Your name]"
- Business justification: "Required to [task] to deliver [project]. Expected duration: [days/weeks]."
- Owner: [manager name]
- Expiration: [YYYY-MM-DD]

B) Change Request summary (short):
- Title: "CR: [Service] - [Short summary]"
- Impact: "No customer-facing downtime expected."
- Rollback: "Revert to previous deploy using tag [vX.Y.Z]"
- Verification: "Smoke tests passing, latency within 10% baseline"

C) Vendor intake minimum (checklist):
- Business sponsor, use case, data classification, anticipated spend, contract owner, security questionnaire attached

D) Expense submission sample text:
- "Flight to SF for QBR (dates): $XXX. Attached receipts. Approved by [manager]."

---

Appendix: Useful links and references

- RBAC and access catalogue: /confluence/security-and-compliance/rbac-and-auth
- Procurement portal: /confluence/finance-and-legal/procurement
- Change management system: internal ticketing link (Change Management)
- Data classification policy: /confluence/security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention

Revision history

- 2024-11-12: Initial draft (Aisha Patel)
- 2025-01-15: Added canary thresholds and temporary escalation template (reviewer: Jordan Rivera)
- 2025-03-18: Incorporated procurement threshold clarification and travel per-night table update (reviewer: Sofia Martinez)

Contact

For clarifications or exemptions, contact people-ops@redwood.com or open an intake ticket using the People Ops form.

End of document
